stock.counterargument: Growth decelerated against the previous quarter, so the trend in the numbers is already turning.
invalidation: Quarterly revenue growth falling below +47.9%, the rate it was running at the quarter before.
Cash conversion dropping below 1.0×, meaning earnings stop being backed by cash.
A close below the 200-session average, which stood at $20.38 on the decision date.
risks: The most recent filing covers a period ending 2026-10-29, 7 days before the decision date.
One of the four quarters in the trailing year is the fourth quarter, which companies report only as part of the full year; it is derived as the annual figure less the first three quarters.
Point-in-time fundamentals are built from filings accepted up to 2026-11-05.

earnings.basis: the same fiscal quarter's announcement a year earlier (2026-02-24) plus 364 days

stock.rule: Universe: every US-listed common stock on NYSE, Nasdaq or NYSE American — about 4,700 names from Nasdaq Trader's own file. Eligible means: priced at $5 or more, median daily turnover of $20M or more over 60 sessions, at least 253 sessions of history, a 10-Q or 10-K whose period ended within 200 days, close above the 200-session average, volatility inside the day's 85th percentile, debt no more than 6× operating cash flow, no results announced in the last 2 sessions, and no position already open in the stock or a fourth in the same SIC division. Eligible candidates are then ranked on equally weighted z-scores within their sector group, over the signals that are defined for that group. One position per session, held 21 sessions, a twenty-first of capital each, 10 basis points of cost each way. Fundamentals are read as they stood on the decision date, never as they read today. The score is a ranking position among that day's eligible candidates. It is not a probability, a price target, or a forecast of any return.
stock.validation: The held-out window has not been opened. No claim of an edge is made or implied.

stories.title: Two dead after bus crashes in France, officials say
stories.excerpt: One child and one young adult were killed in the crash, local authorities say, with more injured.
stories.lead:
One child and one young adult have died after a bus crashed in eastern France, local authorities have said.

The bus was travelling between Lyon and Bourg-en-Bresse when it crashed at around 07:00 local time on Friday in the town of Lent, around 34 miles (55km) from the border with Switzerland.

The town's mayor Yves Cristin told French media the bus "left the road and hit a tree in the ditch".

stories.title: Past White House adviser Raj Panjabi has written a playbook for 'living room' crises
stories.excerpt: Dr. Raj Panjabi is the author of Safer: A Playbook. His goal is to help people face a personal crisis — health, workplace, family conflicts — and "turn fear into action."
stories.lead:
Dr. Raj Panjabi's new book has a simple title: Safer: A Playbook.

Yes, a playbook like the kind sports managers use to firm up a winning strategy. But playbooks aren't just for games.

"In the intensive care unit, we have a playbook when someone's heart stops beating," And when he was a White House health adviser during the COVID emergency, he says, "In the Situation Room, we had a playbook for pandemic preparedness."

stories.title: France takes to the streets again in massive protests over purchasing power
stories.excerpt: Across France, 193 rallies brought together 1.6 million demonstrators, according to the main trade union, and 575,000, according to the Interior Ministry. Unions joined with high school and university students, Yellow Vest protestors and farmers to demand better pay and defend the right to protest.

stories.title: Low birth rates were emptying public schools. ICE deportations are now making it worse
stories.excerpt: School enrollment was already expected to plunge by 2 million kids by 2030. Education experts say deporting immigrant families, many with school-age children, is making the crisis worse.
stories.lead:
Catch up on what you missed with our Education newsletter, sent weekly.

LOS ANGELES — Long before the Trump administration started deporting hundreds of thousands of immigrants, many with school-age children, public schools nationwide faced a massive and accelerating drop in student enrollment caused mostly by shrinking families.

"Birth rates here in Los Angeles County have been declining for decades, which means fewer children enrolled in our schools," said Kelly Gonez, a board member in the LA Unified School District (LAUSD), the second largest in the country, which lost more than 300,000 students over the last two decades.

stories.title: Kenyan doomsday cult leader given life sentence for murdering 191 people
stories.excerpt: Paul Mackenzie ordered his followers to starve their children to death in a forest so they could "meet Jesus".
stories.lead:
A Kenyan court has sentenced the leader of a doomsday cult, Paul Mackenzie, to life in prison for murdering 191 people, all but one of them children.

Alongside 27 others, Mackenzie was found guilty of the murders for instructing members of his cult to starve their children to death so they could "meet Jesus".

The self-styled pastor was arrested in 2023 after the discovery of more than 400 bodies in shallow graves in Shakahola forest near the Kenyan coast. The sprawling investigation into the cases shocked Kenya and drew international attention.

stories.title: How does it affect me if share prices fall?
stories.excerpt: Changes in the FTSE 100 and other indexes are not just for financial experts, they can affect our lives.
stories.lead:
Major tech firms have seen their stock values fall after a sell-off by investors following the US midterm elections.

The fall in the value of their shares across the world has been blamed on an expectation of a slowdown in AI development, although it comes after sharp rises over recent years.

As companies grow, they may issue shares. Many of the largest companies in the UK have shares which are bought and sold on the London Stock Exchange.

stories.title: Voters under 30 helped drive Tuesday's blue wave
stories.excerpt: Young voters played a large role in Democratic wins in this week's midterms. People under 30 voted blue at much higher rates than in 2024.

stories.title: 'I've taken an extra job to pay for heating oil'
stories.excerpt: People in Sussex say they are taking on extra work and not heating their homes due to oil prices.
stories.lead:
A woman from East Sussex says she is having to take on extra work to pay for the soaring cost of her heating oil.

Sheila Williams, from Golden Cross, has taken on a waitress job for the winter to help her pay her bills.

She said her oil bill had doubled since the start of 2026 and the extra job was needed to help pay for it.

Friday night's winner in Riverside will be guaranteed at least a share of the Big West regular season title.

UC San Diego, California Baptist, and UC Santa Barbara all own 3-1 records in conference play. UC Santa Barbara plays its final Big West regular season game Sunday at Cal State Fullerton.
